description: Per scene of scripts/fixtures/chrome-png-export.sh: at most `pixels` pixels of the port's PNG export may differ from Chrome's by more than `channel` levels in a premultiplied channel (excali_raster::diff). Measured on macOS arm64 with the Chromium of tests/web/package-lock.json: scenes with text allow the pixels measured over 64 levels (32 for the three drawn at a third to a half of the size) plus a quarter and 10, scenes without text none over their measured maximum. `note` says where the difference comes from.

default.note: The basic scene's text `export me` (Excalifont, 20 px). Chrome on macOS rasterizes the glyphs through Skia's CoreText path, which smooths (emboldens) the stems; GlyphText fills the same outlines, shaped from the same vendored face and placed on the same baseline, with tiny-skia's analytic coverage. The differences are the edge pixels of the glyphs, a stroke a fraction of a pixel heavier in Chrome. The rough.js shapes agree to within 8 levels.

frames.note: Frame names and embeddable labels are Helvetica, which upstream never ships (`local:`, ADR-004): Chrome draws the machine's Helvetica, the port Liberation Sans (the generic sans-serif a family without faces falls through to), so the label glyphs differ in shape and width: the long name is cut to the frame's width by each font's measurement, `A frame n...` in Chrome and `A frame na...` in the port. The frame outlines and the rectangle agree to within 1 level.

smiley_embedded_v2.note: The scene is one text element, the emoji U+1F600 in Virgil. No vendored face has it and upstream's emoji family is `local:` Segoe UI Emoji (ADR-004), so Chrome falls back to the system's Apple Color Emoji and the port, which reads no system fonts, draws nothing: every emoji pixel differs. The canvas size and the white background around it are equal.
